subject: Recap: POC success criteria & trial plan - Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: POC success criteria & trial plan - Atlas Payments

Hi Sam -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps to get the POC started. Please confirm or flag anything I missed.

POC objectives (what success looks like)
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for 300-token generation (target for API route used in checkout flows)
- Throughput: sustained 100 requests/sec for typical burst profile (10s windows)
- Cost: target <= $0.0008 / token delivered for production-like workloads after batching/caching
- Quality: >90% intent classification accuracy and <2% hallucination rate on a curated eval set (we'll validate on your prompts)

Ownership & deliverables
- Atlas (Sam): share sample dataset + 500 evaluation prompts + success-weighting for intents by 2028-12-12
- Redwood (Jordan + Marissa): provision dedicated trial environment (hosted trial or Dedicated eval pool) and provide eval harness + instrumentation by 2028-12-15
- Dev/Engineering (Dev Patel): integrate the Atlas test webhook and confirm throughput tests (start 2028-12-18)

Evaluation plan
1) Redwood runs an initial smoke run against your sample prompts to validate latency/throughput within 3 business days of receiving data.
2) Joint quality evaluation on the 500-prompt set - we'll return confusion matrix, per-intent recall, and hallucination checks.
3) Cost modeling after batching and prefix cache tuning; we'll provide expected $/token and ops cost estimates.

Next steps
- Sam: send sample dataset + evaluation prompts (by 12/12)
- Jordan/Marissa: share proposed_trial_plan.pdf and instructions for the eval harness (attached) by EOD 12/05
- Schedule a 30-min sync week of 12/18 to review smoke run results and iterate on prompts

Attachments: proposed_trial_plan.pdf (high-level timeline and responsibilities)

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Redwood Inference - developer-first inference for production

From: Sam Patel <sam@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: POC success criteria & trial plan - Atlas Payments

Jordan -

Appreciate the clear write-up. That aligns with internal expectations. A couple of quick clarifications:
- For latency, 200ms p95 is aggressive but reasonable if you can guarantee batching won't add variance. We'll accept up to 250ms p95 if it's consistently stable.
- For throughput, can you confirm whether the 100 req/sec target assumes warm cache/KV state? Our peak will be 120 req/sec during batch settlement windows.

We'll get you the sample dataset and the 500 prompts by 2028-12-12. For access, please include our infra contact (cvp@atlaspayments.com) on any shared links.

Also, is the eval harness something your team runs, or do you expect Atlas to run it on our side? We prefer Redwood to run it once we provide the data.

Thanks -
Sam
Head of Product, Atlas Payments
sam@atlaspayments.com | +1 (617) 555-0987

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Dec 2028 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: POC success criteria & trial plan - Atlas Payments

Sam -

Thanks. Quick answers below:
- Latency: we can start with p95 target of 200ms and agree a tolerance to 250ms as a fallback. We'll include degradation alerts if p95 crosses 220ms during testing so we can triage quickly.
- Throughput: the 100 req/sec assumes warm caches. For your 120 req/sec peaks, we recommend a short warmup (30s) and we'll provision a slightly larger Dedicated pool for the peak windows in the trial. Dev Patel (cc) will own throughput test runs and capacity sizing.
- Eval harness: Redwood will run the harness on our trial environment. We'll share results (confusion matrices, per-intent metrics, hallucination checks) and a short quality report.

I've attached redwood-eval-harness-instructions.md and the proposed_trial_plan.pdf. I'll also create a HubSpot deal and add the test plan link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Proposed dates (confirmable):
- 2028-12-12: Atlas provides prompts/data
- 2028-12-15: Redwood environment ready & initial smoke run
- 2028-12-18: Joint sync to review smoke results

If that works, I'll send a calendar invite for the 12/18 sync.

Best,
Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@atlaspayments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Dec 2028 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: POC success criteria & trial plan - Atlas Payments

Sam / Jordan -

Looping to confirm internal owners and a couple of practical items from the PM side:
- Internal owners: Jordan (Customer lead) + Dev Patel (Engineering lead). I'll be the escalation contact for any SLA/questions.
- Data handling: please send the sample dataset via the shared Drive link (we have permissions set for cvp@atlaspayments.com). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-id
- Non-prod keys: we'll provision trial API keys scoped to the Atlas trial account and rotate them after the POC.

On success criteria, we'll capture the following as the canonical KPI sheet for the POC (we'll run these automatically and share results):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 measured on 300-token generations (target p95 < 200ms; acceptable up to 250ms)
- Throughput: sustained 100 req/sec (target) and ability to handle 120 req/sec bursts for 60s windows
- Cost modeling: expected $/token after batching; target <= $0.0008/token (we'll provide breakdown)
- Quality: joint evaluation on 500 prompts: intent accuracy, per-intent recall, precision, and hallucination rate (<2%)

If you're good with the dates I'll send the calendar invite for the 12/18 sync and add the HubSpot deal link.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
